subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox prune does not clean up workspace directory

question: Should this focused prune-workspace leak be fixed now with a narrow backend-aware cleanup, or should it wait for the broader managed sandbox lifecycle work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98766?
rationale: Both approaches can solve the user-visible stale workspace leak, but recursive sandbox workspace deletion is destructive state cleanup and the broader lifecycle PR is already changing the same ownership boundary.

options.title: Land narrow prune cleanup
options.body: Fix this bug directly by deleting only eligible non-shared sandbox-owned workspaces after confirmed runtime removal, with regression coverage for container, browser, shared, rw, and active-scope safety.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle PR
options.body: Keep this issue open as acceptance criteria for the managed lifecycle branch and close it only after that PR lands with exact-head proof of prune/workspace cleanup.

options.title: Pause new repair work
options.body: Wait until maintainers resolve the draft lifecycle branch and closed unsafe cleanup attempts before queueing another implementation.

recommendation.title: Land narrow prune cleanup
recommendation.body: Fix this bug directly by deleting only eligible non-shared sandbox-owned workspaces after confirmed runtime removal, with regression coverage for container, browser, shared, rw, and active-scope safety.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the active broader lifecycle path and has the strongest history on the sandbox prune/backend boundary.
